question: How is Geo-SMILE behaving technically across Hull, and how faithful, spatially coherent and reproducible are its explanations?

## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a GeoAI Researcher / Model Analyst,
shown with four stat tiles and two Hull-wide dashboard panels (01, Geo branch: signed
Geo-SMILE coefficient against the exact single-LSOA W1 shift for all 168 LSOAs; 02, Feature
branch: map of the local effect magnitude, |local coefficient|, of the most important feature).
The card is CITY-WIDE: report the main Hull-wide results of both branches and the
explanation-quality evaluation. Do not build the narrative around a single
LSOA; an extreme value may appear only as a property of the distribution. This section replaces
section 14 "Length and form" and its bolding rule. Every other section, including prohibited
claims and the self-check, still applies.

Technical language is expected: exact values, test statistics, correlation values, sign
conventions are allowed. Keep the sign convention exact: the signed Geo coefficient is a
relative contribution to the coalition W1, not a direction of crime change. Do not discuss
spatial clustering (Moran's I, LISA) or ATT Faithfulness on this card; the intervention result
(top 20 against random masking) is intervention impact, not faithfulness.

No repetition: every figure appears ONCE on the card. The panels already print the figures in
researcher_diagnostics.shown_on_panels, so neither tiles nor sections cite them; refer to the
panel instead ("panel 01"). A tile figure is not cited again in the sections, not even its
first number.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters); label is at most 8 words naming the quantity exactly
  (e.g. "Geo surrogate held-out R2"). Use exactly these four, in this order: Geo surrogate R2,
  Geo ATT Accuracy (top 20), neighbour-addition Jaccard, Geo seed rank Spearman.
- "section_01": at most 80 words, how the explanation behaves across Hull: Geo branch (panel 01)
  that the signed ranking tracks the exact shift (value is in panel 01; do not cite it) while
  the absolute ranking does not, what the sign means, and how skewed the single-LSOA shift
  distribution is; Feature branch (panel 02) which feature matters most, in how many LSOAs it
  leads, how its local effect varies across Hull (median against the highest, and where by
  locality), and the location players' global ranks.
- "section_02": at most 80 words, explanation quality NOT on the tiles: Feature surrogate
  fidelity, intervention impact (top 20 against random masking, with its p-value), and Feature
  seed rank Spearman against the Geo branch's; then the limitation that matters most. Do not
  cite any tile value. Mark at least two key terms here (e.g. the intervention result and the
  reproducibility contrast).
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words, from researcher_diagnostics.limitations; not about
  spatial clustering or LISA.

Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry no
markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON, and write your own sentences.

Seed reproducibility means feature_seed_rank_spearman and geo_seed_rank_spearman only; never describe a neighbour-addition value as reproducibility across seeds. Give feature_seed_rank_spearman in section_02 and put geo_seed_rank_spearman and the neighbour-addition Jaccard on tiles only: no figure on a tile may appear again in the text. Wrap every figure as [[n:...]], including a total such as [[n:32]]. When citing the largest local effect, name only the place that has that value. Keep section_01 to at most 70 words, and do not cite the neighbour-addition Jaccard or the Geo ATT Accuracy in either section.

illustrative_narrative.headline: Geo-SMILE's [[t:signed ranking]] tracks exact masking; locally, [[t:six-month crime]] dominates almost everywhere.
illustrative_narrative.section_01: The [[t:signed coefficient]] tracks the exact shift (panel 01); its absolute value does not ([[n:-0.27]]), so the sign marks a relative contribution to the coalition W1. Shifts are skewed: median [[n:0.3]], maximum [[n:8.6]]. In the Feature branch, the [[t:six-month crime average]] leads in [[n:144]] LSOAs; its local effect (panel 02) has a median of [[n:3.9]] but reaches [[n:48.5]] in Old Town. Location players rank only [[n:20]] and [[n:23]] of [[n:32]].
illustrative_narrative.section_02: Feature surrogate fidelity is [[n:0.983]]. Masking the Geo top 20 shifts predictions [[n:1.27]] more than random sets ([[n:0.001]]), an [[t:intervention impact]]. Feature ranks are [[t:less reproducible]] across seeds ([[n:0.69]]) than Geo ranks. Attributions remain associational.
illustrative_narrative.footer: Attributions are associational; local LISA p-values are unadjusted.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch random-donor SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA moves its rows to the centroids of random other Hull LSOAs (50 draws, all other inputs kept), and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. Absolute shifts are larger where predicted crime is higher. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (random-donor design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: random_donor
geo_design.definition: Random-donor design: masking an LSOA moves the coordinates of its rows to the centroid of a random other Hull LSOA (K = 50 draws), all other inputs kept; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the XGBoost model on 30 predictors + easting/northing; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

sign_conventions.local_feature_coefficient: Directional. Masks code a retained player as one and the response is the perturbed minus the original prediction, so a positive value means the area's own value of the feature raises its prediction relative to the masking reference and a negative value lowers it.
sign_conventions.global_feature_coefficient: Not directional: fitted to a non-negative distance; rank by magnitude.
sign_conventions.geo_coefficient: Relative contribution to the coalition response; the sign is not a direction of crime.
sign_conventions.feature_branch_model: One XGBoost model on the substantive predictors plus the centroid coordinates; coordinates are kept at their true values and are not Feature players.

limitations: No RAG / no invented local context.

content.headline: Geo-SMILE's [[t:signed ranking]] closely tracks exact masking; [[t:crime, 6-month average]] dominates local attribution.
content.section_01: The [[t:signed Geo coefficient]] ranking tracks the exact single-LSOA shift (panel 01), but the absolute ranking does not ([[n:-0.27]]), so sign marks relative coalition W1 contribution. Shifts are highly skewed: median [[n:0.3]], maximum [[n:8.6]]. In the Feature branch, [[t:crime, 6-month average]] leads in [[n:145]] LSOAs; its local effect (panel 02) has a median of [[n:4.1]] but reaches [[n:50.4]] in Old Town. Location players rank only [[n:20]] (longitude) and [[n:23]] (latitude) of [[n:32]].
content.section_02: Feature surrogate fidelity is [[n:0.985]]. Masking the Geo top 20 shifts predictions [[n:1.27]] more than random sets ([[n:0.001]]), an [[t:intervention impact]]. Feature ranks are [[t:more reproducible]] across seeds ([[n:0.915]]) than Geo ranks. [[t:Attributions are associational]].
content.footer: Local coefficient magnitudes describe attribution, not effects on crime.
